name: Kleberg Foundation Wildlife, Conservation and Animal Science grants

funder.name: Robert J. Kleberg, Jr. and Helen C. Kleberg Foundation

summary: A Texas family foundation's grants for applied wildlife research and habitat restoration and protection, mainly in the Rio Grande Valley of South Texas. Highly competitive, with priority for past grantees.

geography.label: South Texas, mainly the Rio Grande Valley

reporting: Single-year grants need a final report on completion; multi-year grants need annual interim reports and a final report, including an evaluation of effectiveness, lessons learned and an updated project budget.

calls.label: Spring and fall application windows
calls.recurring: Spring window February 1 to March 31 and fall window August 1 to September 30, deadline at midnight CST.

status.quote: The Foundation has two grant cycles per year. The spring and fall deadlines are posted here.

recurring.quote: Grants Deadline AT MIDNIGHT CST Spring: February 1 - March 31 Fall: August 1 - September 30

applicant_types.quote: The Foundation supports IRS-registered, tax exempt, 501(c)(3) organizations with a public charity status of 509(a)(1) or 509(a)(2), or public universities under section 170(c) of the Internal Revenue Code.

geography.quote: support native wildlife, primarily in the Rio Grande Valley of South Texas.

access.quote: Only online grant applications will be accepted.

window.quote: Grants Deadline AT MIDNIGHT CST Spring: February 1 - March 31 Fall: August 1 - September 30

reporting.quote: Single-year funding initiatives - a final report is due upon completion of the grant period. Multi-year funding initiatives - interim reports are due annually with a final report due upon completion of the grant period.
